newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes touch firmer, market marks time.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes touch firmer, market marks time.

text.p: Gold prices were steady to slightly firmer at the afternoon fixing on Wedndesday as the market marked time ahead of further testimony from U.S. Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan.
Greenspan's comments on Tuesday on the first day of his Humphrey-Hawkins congressional testimony on the state of the U.S. economy effectively stopped gold's nascent rally in its tracks.
He said the U.S. economy was slowing and inflation was under control which sent the bond and stock markets as well as the dollar soaring and pulled any potential investors out of gold.
Gold fixed at $324.90 per ounce up from $324.35 in the morning and $328.25 on Tuesday afternoon.
At the fixing the Comex August contract was $0.50 lower at $325.50.
Dealer said as long as gold was in the mid $320s it was caught in a range and it needed to breach $330.00 to confirm a break on the upside.

That figure was threatened only briefly on Tuesday after news that the South African mining complex Western Areas had bought back 1.6 million ounces of a multi-million ounce hedging programme instituted in 1995.
Western Areas' management said the buy-back was to give the company more benefit from forecast higher gold prices.
Although the Far East was easier overnight, business was two-way with signs of Australian producers taking advantage of higher prices to sell forward.
On the downside gold could expect support at the $321-$322 area which effectively acted as a base late last week for the current rally, dealers said.

More interest centred on the platinum group metals (PGMs) which were relatively volatile after steady rises over the past two weeks as Russia's delayed 1997 shipping programme looked like floundering again.
Adminstrative problems have prevented Russia, the main exporter of palladium and second largest exporter of platinum, from exporting metal since December.
A shipment of palladium arrived in Japan earlier this month but platinum exports have yet to start despite assurances from the export agency Almaz.
"There is metal (palladium) coming out but the Japanese are not getting that much and there are delays with platinum to Japan," one market analyst said.
Platinum prices have risen from under $400 on July 10 to $421.00 on Tuesday before fixing at $416.00 on Wednesday.
Palladium firmed from $162.00 to $200.00 in the same period while borrowing rates have fluctuated but basically held in high double figures.
Silver meanwhile moved with gold and was indicated at $4.30/$4.32, down four cents.
